title: Miller produced amino acids under one set of conditions
summary: The 1953 Science paper is a simulation experiment, not a demonstration of how life began.
body: Stanley L. Miller, "A Production of Amino Acids Under Possible Primitive Earth Conditions" (Science, 1953), reported amino acids from a spark-discharge experiment meant to imitate one picture of the early atmosphere. That is evidence that some building blocks can form abiotically under those conditions. It is not a reconstruction of the origin of life. The origin of life is not settled. Walter Gilbert's 1986 note "Origin of life: The RNA world" is a different proposal, that early genetics was RNA, and it is a proposal.
